Write the FAILING suite for #307. Contract = `cd ~/workspace-app && gh issue view 307` — the BODY is the contract (zero comments). Research = `teams/mvox-dev/memory/research/research-307.json` — it carries the exact HEAD shapes and the LIVE 14-label palette; use REAL palette values in fixtures.

## Where the current code stands (verified at HEAD)
- `fetch-issues.ts`: `GitHubLabel { name?: string }` (no color), `GitHubIssue` has no `closed_at`, `normalizeIssue` maps labels to bare name strings. The REST endpoint already returns `labels[].color` (hex WITHOUT leading `#`) and `closed_at` (string|null, date-time) by default — no request change needed, only types + normalize.
- `render.ts`: `RoadmapIssue.labels: string[]`; `boardOrder` (101-105) = plain open/closed filter concat, NO sort anywhere; `renderLabel` (107-109) = fixed grey chip; closed-dim `opacity:0.6` at :194; head is a plain inline <style>, no CSP — per-chip inline `style` attributes are fine.
- Sub-issues recurse through the SAME `boardOrder`/`renderIssue`/`renderLabel` (render.ts:131) — one change covers both levels; pin the inheritance from fixtures anyway.

## Pins (all from the issue's done-when)
1. **Chips**: background = the label's own colour; text colour derived per chip from the background's RELATIVE LUMINANCE (no fixed text colour); a hairline border so a near-white chip reads as a chip. BOTH named worst cases with the real palette values: `blocked` #b60205 → light text; `wontfix` #ffffff → dark text AND visible border on the white page. A label arriving with NO colour → today's neutral chip, not a throw.
2. **Closed ordering**: `closed_at` fetched and carried; closed group sorted most-recently-finished FIRST; a closed issue with missing `closed_at` sorts LAST, no crash. Research verified live: a reopened-then-closed issue's `closed_at` is the LATEST close — no special case needed, but pin the null case.
3. **Open ordering**: by issue number ASCENDING.
4. **The divider**: an explicit divider between the groups with Estonian headings (Pooleli / Tehtud) — hardcoded literals; this page is outside Paraglide, that is correct here, not a violation of the app's i18n rule. Zero-open and zero-closed edge cases: a heading over an empty group — decide and pin (recommend: omit the heading for an empty group).
5. **Sub-issue inheritance**: children under an epic follow the same in-group ordering and render the same coloured chips — fixture with an epic whose children arrive out of order and carry coloured labels. The divider is TOP-LEVEL ONLY — no Pooleli/Tehtud inside an epic.

## Specs that flip (research enumerated; assertion edits ARE allowed on this issue — the rendering change is the point, unlike #302's rule)
- fetch-issues.spec.ts:36-46 + :48-58 assert `labels` equals `['task','ready']` — become object shapes.
- render.spec.ts has five call sites building `labels` as string[] (214, 225, 282, 284, 288).
- Ordering assertions at render.spec.ts:169-179 and board.spec.ts:126, 171 assert group-boundary/API order — extend to the new sorts.

## Luminance math
No luminance/contrast code exists in the repo. Use the standard WCAG relative-luminance formula (linearized sRGB channels, 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722 weights) in a small pure helper with its own spec; pick a threshold and PIN the two worst cases plus a mid-range colour on each side of it. GitHub's own threshold is undocumented — the choice is the implementer's, stated.

tasks.commitBody: The roadmap board now reads the way its own vocabulary implies. Labels render in their real GitHub colours, with each chip's text colour derived from its background's relative luminance and a hairline border keeping near-white chips visible — the palette spans white to near-black, so a fixed text colour was unreadable at one end or the other. Done issues sit under an explicit divider, ordered by when they were finished rather than when they were filed, which is the reading a changelog wants and closes the gap where last week's ship was indistinguishable from August's. Open issues sit above it in number order, lowest first. The divider carries Estonian headings for the pilot readers, hardcoded deliberately: this page builds outside the app's i18n entirely. Sub-issues inherit all of it through the same ordering and chip code path, so an epic's interior can never disagree with the board around it. A label arriving without a colour falls back to the old neutral chip rather than breaking the build. STATED CHOICES: <GREEN agent fills>.
